notes: Isolates pairwise-consistency scanning over a ~7.7 KB / 100-record synthetic policy register delivered inline (plain mode has no filesystem, so the corpus lives in prompt.md). 50 areas x 2 records each; 49 areas agree and exactly one area (VAULT-7, records POL 62 with MAX 90 and POL 92 with MAX 40) disagrees, so the answer is a single unambiguous triple (area plus both ids). Three fields are required because the id pair alone is guessable-adjacent and the area alone is retrievable without comparison. Distractors are consistent near-miss areas (VAULT-1, VAULT-70, VAULT7, each agreeing with itself) so fuzzy area matching lands on the wrong pair, and the true pair sits mid-file and non-adjacent (positions 62 and 92 of 100) so boundary/adjacency shortcuts fail. Tier 1: scan plus exact pairwise compare; strong-model prior >= 90%. Grading scope: final 'FINAL:' line only; ids must be ascending. False-positive audit: (a) a near-miss area pair, (b) reversed id order, (c) a consistent pair, (d) no FINAL line - all rejected.
